prompt:
Use case: identity-preserving spacecraft concept variation. Develop ONE new complete concept directly from the FIRST attached image, the user's preferred BF02 pirate freighter. This is a close development of THAT long-nosed, bilaterally symmetric design, not a generic new freighter.

REFERENCE ROLES IN ORDER:
1 — BF02 is the PRIMARY DESIGN authority for the entire ship: LONG POINTED NOSE, small cabin, forward neck, diagonal cargo cheeks, cargo hump, compact lower keel, three-engine arrangement, short wings, palette and presentation.
2 — Actual native BW freighter cabin close-ups: immutable cabin shell, framing, three glass panes and native size. This reference governs the CABIN ONLY, not the length of the projecting nose blade outside it.
3 — Native freighter clay views: mechanical relationships and overall cargo-ship identity ONLY. Do not revert BF02's redesigned hull or shorten its long pointed nose to this older model.

HIGHEST PRIORITY — BF02 NOSE + MIRROR SYMMETRY:
Preserve the ENTIRE BF02 long forward silhouette in every drawing. A long low sharply tapering polygonal nose blade projects in front of the SMALL cockpit; behind the cockpit a slender solid neck joins the tall cargo shoulder. The complete narrow forward assembly from nose tip to cargo rise occupies roughly 40–45% of total ship length, as BF02 SIDE and TOP show. The taper in FRONT of the cabin is conspicuous, approximately 15–20% of total length, not a tiny stump. Keep BF02's long tip, not a blunt short rectangular snout. Do not enlarge the cabin or move it backward to fake a long nose. Forebody and nose proportions remain fixed across the new variants; the specific design exploration happens BEHIND the cabin.
BILATERAL SYMMETRY is mandatory: mirror the body planes, cheek recesses, paired wing shape, root position, engine pods, mounts and major donor panel layout exactly across the longitudinal center plane. No one-sided armor, different engines, asymmetric cutouts or mismatched wing tips. In the TOP view, near and far sides are exact mirrored silhouettes. REAR view symmetrical around central engine and keel. Perspective may foreshorten, never change actual sizes. Salvage construction can use varied panel types along the length, but always in matched left/right pairs.

IMMUTABLE CABIN:
The original low angular cabin module stays intact, including entire enclosing shell and three glass panes shown by reference 2. Long central pane climbs the sloping crown and is visible from above, plus two side panes. No new crossbar, additional glazing, round canopy, solid roof over central glass, fighter-sized cabin or flat windshield. Native glass size 2.38 wide × .887 high × 2.19 long: remains SMALL relative to the cargo ship. The long nose blade is external forebody ahead of this module and does not authorize cabin alteration. Keep the original small under-nose chin fin.

COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION:
A functional compact Freelancer (2003) pirate/scavenger cargo ship. Retain BF02's tall chamfered central cargo hump, strong diagonal recessed side cheeks, stout closed lower keel, short mid-aft wings and exactly THREE aft-facing engines: one large centerline main nozzle and two smaller low side pods, their exhaust planes slightly forward of the main nozzle. Rear forms a triangle. Pods attach to fixed hull with visible broad solid saddles, not to moving wings. Their FRONT faces are solid service covers or shallow intake slots, visibly different from the recessed rear exhausts.
Short wings use native linear translation inward 2.5 / up .1 / aft 1.0 to stow, not rotating hinges. Preserve native mid-aft root region and provide enclosed receiving pockets and a seam separating each moving wing from fixed hull.
Cargo has two upper central leaves opening outward/upward 45 degrees. The hatch occupies a small central area about 4.82 units long, not the whole roof; preserve its two leaves and clear sweep, no fixed structure bridging them. Show CLOSED hatch, EXTENDED wings in all five drawings. No landing gear or cargo ramp.
Vary specific hull cuts and transitions as the brief directs, while keeping BF02 proportions and a clean long-nose silhouette. No high stacked cargo towers, broad fat transport hull, shallow fighter hull, horizontal multilayer BF01 redesign, or massive center engine that swallows the stern.

SCAVENGER STYLE:
A maintained rebuild from compatible donor sections, with meaningful angular planes, deep backed service recesses, medium-scale mechanical slats, substantial joints and fitted shell transitions. Same complexity as BF02, neither detail carpet nor blank primitive. Pale worn metal, restrained paired ochre patches, dark recessed mechanisms. No heavy peeling/rust blanket or ripped hull. No exposed pipes/cables, skeleton frames, cages, thin rods, decorative frameworks, hanging chains, spikes, skulls or demonic motifs. No modeled rivets, weapons or bolt-on cargo containers. Form changes must read without color changes.

SHEET:
Warm ivory LANDSCAPE 3:2 board matching BF02. Upper left LARGE complete FRONT 3/4, upper right LARGE complete REAR 3/4, lower row SIDE + TOP + REAR orthographic. EVERY perspective shows the entire ship including the long pointed nose, both wing-tip extents, keel and engine mounts inside margins. Full design, never only the stern. TOP must be a true flat overhead projection with exact mirrored edges, nose left; no perspective masquerading as top. Same structure and proportions in all views, identical cabin scale and engine count. Clear neutral lighting, no scenery or flames, no alternate ships within the sheet. Title contains the new variant ID; simple view labels.

VARIANT BF28 — Шевронные углубления:
Shape each cargo flank's large service field as a broad CLOSED recessed chevron, its two slanted ends joined by a solid horizontal middle wall. This is a shallow V in the boundary of a backed mechanical pocket, not a hole or decoration attached outside. Use three broad inset cooling slats in the rear half, quiet flat access panels in the forward half. The lower chevron edge transitions directly into the engine support. Preserve BF02's overall diagonal-shoulder silhouette, symmetrical long nose and calm cargo roof.

Title: "BW PIR FREIGHTER / BF28". This must remain unmistakably the SYMMETRICAL LONG-NOSED BF02 with the specified changes behind the cabin. Render a coherent whole design in all five views.
